# 🔭 linkwatch **Keep an eye on your websites from the terminal.** A small, friendly link & uptime checker: list your sites in one file, run one command, and get a live status table plus a clean HTML status page you can host anywhere. ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white) ![Interface](https://img.shields.io/badge/interface-CLI-4B4B4B?logo=gnubash&logoColor=white) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/docker-ready-2496ED?logo=docker&logoColor=white) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green) [Quick start](#-quick-start) • [Usage](#-usage) • [Configuration](#%EF%B8%8F-configuration) • [How it works](#-how-it-works) • [Tests](#-running-the-tests)
--- ## ✨ Features - 📋 **One config file**: list every site you care about in `sites.toml` - ⚡ **Live terminal table**: watch results fill in as each site is checked - 🟢 **Clear status**: UP/DOWN, HTTP status code, response time and page title - 🕒 **Last-Modified tracking**: see when a page was last updated (when the server reports it) - 💾 **Cached results**: the last run is saved, so you can build reports any time - 🌐 **HTML status page**: one command turns your results into a shareable `status.html` - 🐳 **Docker ready**: run everything without touching your local Python --- ## 🖥️ Preview ```text $ python -m linkwatch.cli check My sites ┏━━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━┳━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓ ┃ Site ┃ Status ┃ Code ┃ Time ┃ Title ┃ ┡━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┩ │ Python │ UP │ 200 │ 113 ms │ Welcome to Python.org │ │ PyPI │ UP │ 200 │ 59 ms │ PyPI · The Python Package Index │ │ Example │ UP │ 200 │ 204 ms │ Example Domain │ │ GitHub │ UP │ 200 │ 236 ms │ GitHub │ └─────────┴────────┴──────┴────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘ 4/4 sites up, results saved to ~/.cache/linkwatch/results.json ``` --- ## 🚀 Quick start You only need **one** of the two options below. ### Option A: Docker (no Python setup needed) ```bash git clone https://github.com/rishrek/linkwatch.git cd linkwatch make docker-build docker run --rm -it linkwatch python -m linkwatch.cli check ``` ### Option B: Local Python 3.12 ```bash git clone https://github.com/rishrek/linkwatch.git cd linkwatch make setup # creates .venv and installs everything (one time) source .venv/bin/activate # do this in every new terminal python -m linkwatch.cli check ```
On Windows, or without make? ```powershell py -3.12 -m venv .venv .venv\Scripts\activate pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt python -m linkwatch.cli check ``` If your Python 3.12 has a different name on macOS/Linux, pass it to make: `make setup PYTHON=/path/to/python3.12`
--- ## 📖 Usage | Command | What it does | |---------|--------------| | `python -m linkwatch.cli check` | Checks every site, shows the live table and saves the results | | `python -m linkwatch.cli report` | Builds `status.html` from the last saved results | | `python -m linkwatch.cli info` | Shows where the templates and cached results live | | `python -m linkwatch.cli --help` | Lists all commands and options | ### Options | Command | Option | Default | Description | |---------|--------|---------|-------------| | `check` | `--config PATH` | `sites.toml` | Use a different sites file | | `report` | `-o, --output PATH` | `status.html` | Where to write the HTML page | | `report` | `--title TEXT` | `linkwatch` | Heading shown on the status page | ### A typical session ```bash python -m linkwatch.cli check # 1. check your sites python -m linkwatch.cli report -o status.html # 2. build the status page open status.html # 3. view it (xdg-open on Linux) ``` --- ## ⚙️ Configuration All sites live in **`sites.toml`** in the project folder: ```toml title = "My sites" [[sites]] name = "Python" url = "https://www.python.org" [[sites]] name = "Example" url = "https://example.com" ``` | Key | Required | Description | |-----|----------|-------------| | `title` | no | Heading shown above the terminal table | | `[[sites]]` | yes | One block per site you want to check | | `name` | yes | Short label for the site | | `url` | yes | Full address, must start with `http://` or `https://` | To add a site, copy a `[[sites]]` block and change the name and URL. ### Where results are stored | System | Location | |--------|----------| | macOS | `~/Library/Caches/linkwatch/results.json` | | Linux | `~/.cache/linkwatch/results.json` | | Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\linkwatch\linkwatch\Cache\results.json` | Set the `LINKWATCH_CACHE_DIR` environment variable to keep results somewhere else. --- ## 🧠 How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR A["sites.toml"] -->|"check"| B["Live table in terminal"] A -->|"check"| C[("results.json cache")] C -->|"report"| D["status.html"] ``` 1. **Load**: `sites.toml` is read and validated (every site needs a name and a valid URL). 2. **Check**: each site gets an HTTP GET request, and linkwatch records the status code, response time, page title and `Last-Modified` header. 3. **Save**: results are written as JSON to your cache folder. 4. **Report**: the saved results are rendered into a standalone HTML page with a summary of what's up and what's down. ### Project structure ```text linkwatch/ ├── linkwatch/ │ ├── cli.py # commands: check, report, info │ ├── config.py # reads and validates sites.toml │ ├── checker.py # visits each site and collects results │ ├── encoding.py # page charset detection and title extraction │ ├── dates.py # Last-Modified parsing │ ├── http_patch.py # default request headers │ ├── cache.py # saves and loads results.json │ ├── report.py # builds the HTML status page │ ├── resources.py # locates the bundled templates │ └── templates/ │ └── status.html.j2 ├── tests/ # pytest suite with a tiny local test server ├── sites.toml # your list of sites ├── requirements.txt # app dependencies ├── requirements-dev.txt # test dependencies ├── Dockerfile └── Makefile ``` --- ## 🧪 Running the tests The tests start a tiny local web server, so they don't depend on real websites. ```bash make test # locally (activate .venv first) make docker-test # inside Docker (run make docker-build first) ``` ### Make targets | Target | Description | |--------|-------------| | `make setup` | Create `.venv` and install all dependencies | | `make test` | Run the pytest suite | | `make test-nose` | Run the suite with nose | | `make docker-build` | Build the Docker image | | `make docker-test` | Run the tests inside Docker | --- ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, bug reports and pull requests are welcome. Fork the repo, create a branch, and open a PR. Please run `make test` before submitting. ## 📄 License Released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
